text:
eli: FYI onboarding LlamaX-7B. The HF repo includes a generation_config.json that looks inconsistent and I want to be sure we map params to Redwood the right way. snippet:

```json
{
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "top_p": 0.95,
  "top_k": 50,
  "repetition_penalty": 1.2,
  "do_sample": false,
  "max_new_tokens": 256
}
```

eli: Quick questions — 1) does do_sample=false mean top_p/top_k are ignored? 2) temperature=0 but top_p>0 looks contradictory. 3) Redwood uses max_tokens vs HF max_new_tokens — any gotchas? :eyes:

mari: short answer: yes, do_sample=false usually forces greedy, ignoring sampling params. temperature=0 == deterministic/greeedy in most runtimes. top_p/top_k only matter when sampling enabled.

ashok: add nuance: some HF configs set sampling params even when do_sample=false (they're just leftovers). We should prefer an explicit mapping policy: if do_sample is false OR temperature==0 -> set Redwood sampling_mode="greedy" and drop top_p/top_k.

ashok: about repetition_penalty: HF applies it as a multiplicative penalty on token scores (score[token] /= penalty if repeated). Redwood historically implemented an additive logit bias in one runtime path. For onboarding, best to keep the HF rp value but run a small eval set — there can be a ~0.2-0.5 BLEU-style QA change if you blindly copy.

eli: good to know. Any conversion snippet we can use in onboarding scripts?

mari: here's a pragmatic mapper we use in the eval harness (pseudo):

```python
# generation_config -> redwood request (conceptual)
def hf_to_redwood(g):
    rd = {}
    if g.get('do_sample') is False or (g.get('temperature') is not None and g['temperature'] == 0.0):
        rd['mode'] = 'greedy'
        rd['temperature'] = 0.0
        rd['top_p'] = None
        rd['top_k'] = None
    else:
        rd['mode'] = 'sampling'
        rd['temperature'] = g.get('temperature', 1.0)
        rd['top_p'] = g.get('top_p')
        rd['top_k'] = g.get('top_k')
    # repetition_penalty: keep the number but flag for eval check
    rd['repetition_penalty'] = g.get('repetition_penalty', 1.0)
    # HF max_new_tokens -> Redwood max_tokens (redwood expects new tokens count)
    rd['max_tokens'] = g.get('max_new_tokens') or g.get('max_tokens')
    return rd
```

mari: note: we explicitly set top_p/top_k to None for greedy so downstream runtime doesn't try to sample.

ashok: also watch special tokens: HF sometimes uses 'pad_token_id'==eos_id or 0; if the tokenizer has no pad token, some HF generation code falls back to eos. For Redwood private deployments we always require explicit pad_token_id mapping. When you convert, assert tokenizer.pad_token_id is not None or set pad_token_id = eos_token_id to match HF behaviour but record it in onboarding notes.

sara: regarding chat templates — HF chat models often have 'system'/'user' role tokens baked into preprocess. Redwood expects clean messages (role + content) and will apply our chat-format templates. If the HF repo already wraps messages in "<s>[INST]...", don't double-wrap. Typical bug: config.generation has prompt_template that includes role labels and model also expects roles -> you get duplicated role tokens. Onboarding checklist item.

eli: good call. I'll grep the repo for common wrappers like "<s>" "[INST]" "</s>" and for explicit role handling.

eval-bot: automated note: please run the micro-regression suite (qa-prompts-small) after param mapping. Threshold: no more than 1% drop in pass@1 or else flag for manual tuning.

mari: one more edge case: top_k==0 in some HF configs means "no top_k". But some code treats 0 as keep 0 tokens -> catastrophic. Map top_k <= 0 -> None. Same for top_p <= 0 or top_p >= 1.0 -> interpret as disabled (None).

ashok: reproduction tip: if you see weird repetition after mapping rp=1.2, run with rp=1.0 and sampling on to confirm it's the rp causing issues vs tokenizer mismatch. Often when we quantize to int8, repetition behavior changes slightly because logits are noisier; don't assume mapping is perfect.

eli: action items for this thread: 1) I'll add hf_to_redwood mapper to onboarding scripts. 2) run micro-regression via eval-bot. 3) add pad_token/assertion and prompt-template grep.

sara: I can pair for the prompt/template grep tomorrow.

eli: thanks — will ping once initial runs are in. :thumbsup:
